key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films are not just defects—they are chemically validated failure initiation sites that enable early degradation detection.
engineering_relevance: A fast, non-invasive microscopy-plus-ML screening workflow can pre-qualify perovskite films for scalable, stability-critical solar cell manufacturing.
method: Nano-FTIR identified impurity chemistry in the films
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy captured impurity patterns quickly
Machine learning quantified impurity density and enabled rapid screening
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation starts at impurity–perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density degraded faster in early-stage stability tests.
watch_item: The diagnostic value depends on imaging quality and calibration to the specific film stack, composition, and processing conditions.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
